confirmed: The source is arXiv:2601.12152v1 dated 17 January 2026, a 32-page preprint with embedded Appendices A-F; source.version, title, and all six listed authors match the PDF (p. 1; appendices pp. 23-32). The entire local markdown was read, including the appendices.

S1 has explicit individual random assignment to Low, Medium, or Intensive AI control and individual proposal production in supervised Zoom sessions with screen sharing. lab_rct is supported under the supervised-session definition, and this is a comparison of AI configurations (pp. 11-12, Sections 5.1-5.2; p. 8, Table 3).

S1 reports 54 recruited researchers with allocation of 18 per condition, followed by 51 retained quantitative cases, 17 per condition. These are people, not proposals or ratings; the analyzed sample is above the 50-person threshold (p. 12, Section 5.2; p. 13, Section 5.3.1).
The recruited population is reported as 40 PhD students, seven postdoctoral fellows, and seven professors or research scientists, supporting population mixed (p. 12, Section 5.2).

Unique_research_proposals is described as participants' proposal production and supports a fluency outcome under the codebook; it is sufficient to retain the randomized study for two-screener review. It does not establish rated novelty, quality, or diversity of the main-study proposals (p. 13, Section 6.1; p. 14, Table 4; p. 29, Appendix C.2; creativity-codebook.md, Sections 3 and 6).

Every number in S1-O1 reported matches Table 4: Intensive 1.58 (0.77), Medium 1.88 (1.20), Low 2.19 (1.11), F(2, 48) = 1.52, p = 0.22. The caption specifies means and SDs of frequencies per hour, and the test is omnibus (p. 14, Table 4).

Every number in one_line_finding matches: 51 analyzed; proposal-production F(2, 48) = 1.52, p = 0.22; weighted CSI means Intensive 63.20, Low 59.65, Medium 53.13; Kruskal-Wallis chi-square 2.08, df 2, p = 0.353. CSI is explicitly post-task self-report, not a creativity score on the produced proposals (p. 12, Section 5.3.1; p. 13, outlier paragraph; p. 14, Tables 4-5).

The main system used GPT-4.1 for Ideator and Writer and Claude Sonnet 3.7 for Evaluator; the notebook interface excluded chat and provided the recorded control-level features (p. 8, Table 3 and Section 3.3.1; p. 10, Section 3.3.2).

The form correctly preserves the duration discrepancy: approximately 35-40 minutes of proposal generation within an approximately 90-minute session in the main procedure, versus 30 minutes in the task script (pp. 11-12, Section 5.1; p. 29, Appendix C.2).

S2 is a model-output pilot with two PhD providers/evaluators and ten seed-idea comparisons, using GPT-4o-mini and the named Claude 3.7, DeepSeek-V3, and Gemini 2.0 judges. Its reported human preferences exactly match the PDF: four RAG, two non-RAG, four undecided; no randomized people comparison is stated (pp. 27-28, Appendix B.1 and Table 6).

S3 is a separate model-output pilot with three researchers: two PhD students and a physics postdoctoral fellow. The reported proposed-system versus Deep Research ranks are exactly 3 versus 1, 2 versus 1, and 2 versus 1 for ideas 11-13; models and the early-June-2025 timing match Table 7. No random assignment of people or order is stated (pp. 27-28, Appendix B.2 and Table 7).

S4 describes formative within-person testing, more than two hours on average and a five-minute break, without a separate analyzed count or stated randomized condition order. The four external design collaborators cannot be treated as a reported S4 analyzed sample; the two- and three-person system pilots are not added to S1 (p. 4, Section 3.1; p. 11, Section 4.2; p. 27, Appendix B).

The classifications S2/S3 model_only, S4 other, and eligibility.context_class none are supported: there is no AI-versus-human-output, observational adoption, or synthesis study here. Synthesis defaults appropriately contain no pooled estimates or study totals (pp. 11-14, Sections 4-6; pp. 27-28, Appendix B).
summary: The randomized AI-configuration study analyzed 51 researchers and reported proposal fluency, supporting two-screener review. All reported numerical results match the PDF, but company involvement and several structured count, exclusion, timing, and comparison fields need correction.
